full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J. This Civil petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 11.08.2010 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 22 of 2005 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 01.09.2004 passed by the learned Joint District judge, Third Court, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 214 of 1994 decreeing the suit on contest against defendant No. 1 and dismissing the suit ex-parte against defendant No. 2. The facts, giving rise to this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal in brief, are; 

 4. The trial Court upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 01.09.2004 decreed the suit on contest against defendant No. 1 and dismissed the suit ex-parte against defendant No. 2. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, defendant No. 1 preferred First Appeal No. 22 of 2005 before the High Court Division. The learned judges of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties by the judgment and order dated 11.08.2010 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 10. On considerations of exhibits-3 and 4, the High Court Division found that delivery of goods was made on 17.02.1993 in presence of the appellant and the respondent and that the shortage of goods was detected in their presence. The High Court Division held that it was unable to accept the submissions of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the wagons with seals and intact rivets were handed over to the port authority after arrival at Chittagong Port and that Railway Authority was not involved with the unloading of wagons in question. The High Court division came to a finding that from the loading point to the delivery points, the goods were under the care and control of the appellant-petitioner being entrusted as per minutes dated 06.01.1990 and the Railway Receipts (R.P.) and that in the circumstances, the appellant carrier was solely responsible for the loss of the goods and therefore liable to pay compensation for the said loss. The High Court Division was of the view that the learned Joint District Judge, Third Court, Chittagong on consideration of materials on record properly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff-company.
